::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

The alternating harmonic series converges to $\ln 2$:
$$
  \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} \frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k} = 1 - \frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} - \ldots = \ln 2.
$$

1. Implement the function `partial_sums(n)`, which returns the vector of the partial sums $s_1, \ldots, s_n$.

1. Compute the errors of $s_{10}$, $s_{100}$ and $s_{1000}$. How many terms are needed for one more correct digit?
   Compare with the geometric series from @exr-geometric.

::: {.lm-scaffold}
```{r}
partial_sums <- function(n) {
  # ...
}
```
:::

::: {.lm-solution}
```{r}
partial_sums <- function(n) {
  k <- 1:n
  cumsum((-1)^(k + 1) / k)
}

sums <- partial_sums(1000)
ns <- c(10, 100, 1000)
data.frame(n = ns, error = abs(sums[ns] - log(2)))
```

The error is about $1 / (2n)$: one more correct digit needs ten times as many terms. The geometric series with
$q = 1/10$ gains one digit with each term.
:::
:::
